collections.title: Comedy · Traditions and Modern Approaches
collections.summary: An introduction to rival explanations and several comic traditions, followed by a map of modern approaches.

collections.title: Comedy · Linguistic, Cognitive, and Philosophical Theories
assumed_background: The orientation introduces the competing questions; no formal logic or psychology course is assumed.

collections.title: Comedy · Publics, Politics, and Comic Selves
assumed_background: General audience; theories are compared rather than treated as universal laws.

collections.title: Comedy · Improvisation and Ensemble Writing
assumed_background: No performance training required; examples introduce the practical vocabulary.

collections.title: Comedy · Stand-Up, Clown, and Sitcom
assumed_background: General audience; technique and cultural institution are kept distinct.

collections.title: Comedy · Language, Translation, and Reception
assumed_background: No second language required; examples distinguish linguistic and cultural knowledge.

collections.title: Comedy · Absurdism, Surrealism, and Anti-Comedy
assumed_background: The traditions and modern map supply context, while individual lectures establish their works.
